England.difference_en: England begins with halves and quarters in Year 1 using objects, shapes and quantities. In the verified revised PEP sequence, fraction meaning is introduced explicitly in Grade 3 upper semester through ‘Initial Understanding of Fractions’, then developed further through Grades 5–6.
England.why_en: Part-whole models are intuitive, but equal partitioning must be explicit.
England.classroom_use_en: Show equal and unequal partitions and ask which genuinely represent one quarter.

US.difference_en: Common Core Grades 1-2 build equal-share experience in geometry; Grade 3 formally develops fractions as numbers.
US.why_en: Equal-part experience can precede the shift from 'part of a shape' to a number with magnitude.
US.classroom_use_en: After shading a fraction, represent the same fraction on a number line.

England.difference_en: England progressively represents fractions on number lines and in measurement/quantity contexts through Key Stage 2.
England.why_en: Treating fractions as measurable numbers supports comparison, equivalence and fractions greater than 1.
England.classroom_use_en: For each new fraction, include at least one question asking where it lies on a number line.

US.difference_en: Common Core Grade 3 defines 1/b using equal intervals on a number line from 0 to 1.
US.why_en: The denominator defines the size of the unit and the numerator counts those units.
US.classroom_use_en: Describe 3/4 as three units of 1/4 before locating it.

England.difference_en: England connects fractions with division and proportional relationships in the upper primary years.
England.why_en: a/b can represent both a collection of unit fractions and the result of a divided by b.
England.classroom_use_en: Share 3 pizzas among 4 people and connect 3÷4 with 3/4.

US.difference_en: Common Core Grade 5 explicitly interprets a fraction as division of the numerator by the denominator.
US.why_en: This connects fraction notation with division, ratio and later algebra.
US.classroom_use_en: Explain 3/4 both as three 1/4 units and as 3÷4.

England.difference_en: England develops unit fractions progressively from Year 1 and uses them to compose non-unit fractions.
England.why_en: A unit fraction provides a countable unit: 3/5 is three copies of 1/5.
England.classroom_use_en: When reading 3/5, ask what the unit fraction is and how many such units there are.

US.difference_en: Common Core Grade 3 defines 1/b as a fundamental fraction unit and a/b as a copies of that unit.
US.why_en: Unitising fractions parallels unitising in whole-number place value and connects well with current PEP emphasis on counting units.
US.classroom_use_en: Compare 'four tens' with 'four one-fifths' as examples of counting mathematical units.

England.difference_en: England explicitly places fractions on number lines from Year 3 and later extends this to improper fractions and decimals.
England.why_en: Number lines show order, distance and fractions greater than 1, which area models alone do not always make clear.
England.classroom_use_en: Give only 0 and 1 and ask pupils to decide how the interval should be partitioned.

US.difference_en: Common Core Grade 3 makes the number line part of the formal definition of fractions.
US.why_en: This directly reinforces the idea that a fraction is a number and gives equivalence a shared location.
US.classroom_use_en: Explain equivalent fractions as the same point before introducing a symbolic rule.

England.difference_en: England begins simple equivalence in Year 2, develops families of equivalent fractions in Year 4, and uses equivalence in later comparison and calculation.
England.why_en: Equivalence means the quantity is unchanged while the fraction unit/partition changes.
England.classroom_use_en: Place 1/2, 2/4 and 4/8 at the same position on one number line.

US.difference_en: Common Core begins simple fraction equivalence in Grade 3 and requires visual-model explanations and generation of equivalent fractions in Grade 4.
US.why_en: The structural relationship is established before multiplying numerator and denominator is treated as a compressed procedure.
US.classroom_use_en: Before teaching the symbolic rule, justify 1/2=2/4 with a model or number line.
